title: Gold, Silver, Platinum Import Tax Relief Ends: What It Means for Buyers
description: The Indian government has withdrawn the upfront IGST exemption for banks and nominated agencies importing precious metals. This means importers now pay IGST a.

faq.q: What is the new 3% customs levy on precious metals?
faq.a: The 3% customs levy is a new additional duty imposed on the import of gold, silver, and platinum by nominated agencies and banks, effective April 1, 2026. It adds to the existing basic customs duties.

faq.q: How does the withdrawal of upfront IGST exemption affect buyers?
faq.a: While the upfront IGST exemption withdrawal primarily impacts the working capital of importers, the 3% customs levy is a direct cost increase that will likely be passed on to the end consumer, leading to higher retail prices.

faq.q: Will gold prices in India increase significantly?
faq.a: The 3% customs levy will directly increase the landed cost of precious metals. While other market factors also influence prices, this change introduces a definite upward pressure on domestic prices for gold, silver, and platinum.

faq.q: Are Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) affected by these changes?
faq.a: SGBs are not directly affected as they are financial instruments. However, their pricing is linked to the domestic market price of gold, which could see an indirect impact if physical gold prices rise due to the new levies.

faq.q: Does this apply to all types of gold purchases?
faq.a: Yes, this change impacts the import cost of the raw precious metal. Therefore, any physical purchase of gold, silver, or platinum in India, whether jewellery, coins, or bars, will likely reflect these increased costs.

faq.q: Where can I find official government notifications on these tax changes?
faq.a: Official notifications regarding customs duties and GST are typically published by the Ministry of Finance and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).

fact_check.summary: The article accurately reports on the withdrawal of IGST exemption and the introduction of a new customs levy on precious metal imports, with correct dates and percentages. However, it misrepresents the nature of the "new 3% customs levy" as distinct from IGST.
